title: 0364-deep-learning-for-sports-video-event
universal_lens: Action spotting and precise event detection unify temporal segmentation with probabilistic event classification via tolerance-window formalism across multi-sport video datasets. Action spotting accuracy metrics (AP) decomposed by tolerance windows (frames/seconds) enable separation of coarse indexing from frame-accurate event localization.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs conformal predictive distributions over frame-precise event timestamps using Bayesian interval regression on annotated sports video data. Bayesian confidence intervals on AP scores per event class allow GSI to calibrate probabilistic event detection thresholds dynamically across tolerance tiers.
gse_mapping: GSE models sport-specific state transitions through discrete event automata, where each detected action triggers probabilistic belief updates in situational awareness. State transitions between video frames indexed via tolerance-windowed AP metrics guide GSE's multimodal fusion engine to select optimal sensor modalities for real-time event confirmation.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 1 introduces foundational concepts for action spotting and precise event detection in sports video analysis. It establishes a taxonomy of datasets and methods that support temporal segmentation and event classification. The core idea revolves around annotating video frames with discrete events such as goals, cards, and ball actions. These annotations form the basis for training machine learning models capable of detecting these events in real-time. The tolerance-window formalism allows for robustness against minor misalignments in event timing. This framework enables downstream applications like highlight generation and tactical analysis. The chapter emphasizes the importance of standardized datasets like SoccerNet-v2 and Tennis E2E-Spot, which provide consistent benchmarks for evaluating performance. By leveraging interval-annotated data, it becomes possible to treat event boundaries as probabilistic thresholds rather than fixed points. This probabilistic treatment enhances adaptability across different sports and contexts. The derived kernel approach maps interval annotations into discrete event sequences, enabling automated reasoning about game dynamics. The multi-sport event taxonomy ensures interoperability between diverse domains while preserving specificity. Overall, this chapter sets the stage for integrating structured event detection into intelligent sports analytics engines.
